title: Bacterial 16S-V4V5 rRNA amplification for NGS Illumina sequencing
author: Estelle Bigeard
materials: PCR products should be checked initially by gel electrophoresis for unspecific amplification and band size. - Check the PCR products on agarose gel to see if the bands are weak or strong. Prepare an agarose gel 1-1.5% in 0.5X TAE buffer Microwave until the solution is clear (2 minutes) Stain with 20 µL ethidium bromide per 100ml (or SYBR-safe dye) Ethidium bromide 10 mg/ml Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #E1510 Be careful : Put labcoat, nitriles gloves! Prepare tray & comb(s) Pour gel into tray When the gel is polymerized, remove comb Load gel in electrophesis cuve containing the same 0.5X TAE buffer Gel must be covered Cut one strip of parafilm. Load 1-2 µL loading dye onto parafilm, one drop per sample Mix 1 to 3 μl of each PCR product with loading dye (up & down 3 times) Load it in the agarose gel Load 3 µL of SmartLadder into first and/or last well. Close & Plug in electrodes to power source Run the migration for ~120 V, 30-45 minutes Observe results using a UV imager like Image Quant LAZ4000, Ge Healthcare The negative control must be negative and the positive control must be positive to validate the PCR. The size of amplicons is approximatly 400 bp. It is possible to obtain some bands of longer size. Figure 2 : 16s DNA PCR amplicons (sample / ladder) - Samples with failed PCRs (or spurious bands) are re-amplified by optimizing the PCR (further template dilution to 1:100 or using BSA/other additives) to produce correct bands, or purified using a purification kit like “Nuclesopin Gel & Clean up kit– Macherey-Nagel”. Amplicons are stored at -20°C until treatment.

steps.title: Extract and quantify nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Extract DNA (or RNA followed by cDNA synthesis) using a kit appropriate for the sample type; quantify the final DNA with NanoDrop or Qubit/PicoGreen, ensuring A260/280 ≥ 1.8 and concentration ≥ 1 ng/µL; avoid extra clean‑ups unless PCR inhibition is observed; optionally run a 0.8 % agarose gel (1 µL DNA + loading buffer, EtBr detection limit ≈10 ng) to check integrity; if DNA is ≥5 ng/µL, dilute to 5 ng/µL with nuclease‑free water (no need to re‑measure), otherwise use the sample as‑is.

substeps.instruction: Extract DNA (or RNA → cDNA) with appropriate kit
Quantify DNA (NanoDrop or Qubit/PicoGreen), check A260/280 ≥ 1.8 and ≥1 ng/µL
Optional gel check: 0.8 % agarose, 1 µL DNA + loading buffer, EtBr
Dilute to 5 ng/µL if concentration ≥5 ng/µL; otherwise proceed directly

steps.title: Prepare Illumina primers
steps.instruction: Order primers (e.g., Eurogentec) with RP‑HPLC purity, 10–40 nmol synthesis scale, supplied at 100 µM in TE; dissolve dried primers in nuclease‑free water or 1× TE to make a 100 µM stock; dilute 1:10 with molecular‑grade water to a 10 µM working solution in a PCR hood; store both stock and working solutions at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Order primers (RP‑HPLC, 10–40 nmol, 100 µM TE)
Reconstitute dried primers to 100 µM stock
Dilute 1:10 to 10 µM working solution in PCR hood
Store stock and working solutions at –20 °C

steps.title: Pilot PCR test with non‑Illumina primers
steps.instruction: Select a few representative samples and set up test PCRs using primers without the Illumina tail (standard purification, e.g., Se‑POP) to optimise conditions; run low‑cycle, high‑initial‑denaturation reactions in triplicate; include a negative control for each series and, if desired, a positive mock‑community control (e.g., Zymo) with known cell/DNA concentration.

substeps.instruction: Choose representative samples
Use tail‑free primers for test PCRs
Run low‑cycle, high‑initial‑denaturation triplicates
Include negative control per series
Optionally include mock‑community positive control

steps.title: Set up final PCR reactions
steps.instruction: In a UV‑sterilised PCR hood, prepare the reaction mix using KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix® according to Table 3; add template DNA (volume adjusted to achieve ~5 ng per reaction, based on the concentration range); set up each sample in triplicate and include a negative control; use an enzyme not derived from bacteria and limit the number of cycles as defined in the thermal profile.

substeps.instruction: Prepare master mix with KAPA HiFi ReadyMix® (Table 3)
Add template DNA (adjust volume for ~5 ng per reaction)
Aliquot reactions in triplicate plus negative control
Keep setup under UV in PCR hood

steps.title: Run thermal cycling
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler with the conditions listed in Table 4 for KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix® (initial denaturation, cycle denaturation, annealing, extension, final extension) and run the PCR.

steps.title: Verify PCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 1 µL of each PCR product with loading buffer onto a 0.8 % agarose gel, run, and visualise with EtBr; the detection limit is ~10 ng; confirm the expected amplicon size and absence of non‑specific bands.

steps.title: Quantify purified PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of purified PCR products using a Nanoquant Plate on a Spark Tecan (2 µL sample) to obtain concentration and 260/280, 260/230 ratios; alternatively, use a Qubit 4 fluorometer for higher precision.

steps.title: Purify and pool triplicate amplicons
steps.instruction: Clean the pooled triplicate PCR products with the Macherey‑Nagel NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit, applying the following modifications: first elution – add 30 µL TE pre‑heated to 70 °C onto the column, incubate 5 min at 70 °C, centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min; second elution – add 30 µL TE (pre‑heated or previous eluate) and centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min; aliquot 2.5 µL for quantification; store the purified pool at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µL TE (70 °C) to column, incubate 5 min at 70 °C
Centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min (first elution)
Add 30 µL TE (pre‑heated or previous eluate), centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min (second elution)
Pool triplicate eluates
Aliquot 2.5 µL for quantification
Store purified pool at –20 °C

steps.title: Submit libraries for sequencing
steps.instruction: Capture gel images to document purity, degradation and band intensity; send the images together with the purified libraries (dry‑ice shipped) to the sequencing platform; follow the platform‑specific library preparation protocol (e.g., Illumina MiSeq 2 × 250 bp, Genomer Platform protocols.io “Preparation of libraries (Metabarcoding) for Illumina sequencing – Genomer Platform”).

substeps.instruction: Take gel photos for quality documentation
Package purified libraries with dry ice
Ship to sequencing facility
Follow facility‑specific library preparation instructions
